title: Pokémon Y
tested: New game in German from the language screen through the professor's talk, the name entry on the touch screen and the bedroom scene; walking around the room, the X menu, saving, and after a restart Continue from that save. Not tested: anything after the bedroom (no battle, no outdoor area), long sessions. Also on a low-budget machine (Batocera Linux mini PC, AMD Ryzen 3 PRO 4350GE, Radeon Vega 6): the same new-game route and the Continue route, started from the system's menu, with a photo of the screen checked for each; 60 shown / 30 game pictures a second once the shaders of a scene are cached. The first time a scene is shown its shaders are compiled, which drops the game to as low as 8 to 20 pictures a second for up to a minute (measured in Pokémon X's opening); the cache is kept. 19 Nov 2026, on the mini PC (Ryzen 3 PRO 4350GE, Radeon Vega 6): hitches measured per picture and three causes fixed in the local patch - pipelines linked at once when their parts exist and remade in the background from a list of the runs before, one worker thread kept for the quick fragment-shader pipelines, the CPU shading a draw until its vertex shader is compiled on integrated GPUs - and the game file read from an SSD instead of a pooled hard disk (each read through the pool cost 8-40 ms and stopped picture and sound). Test routes afterwards: no sound gap, 0-2 late pictures inside a scene. Still open: a scene the game reads back from the GPU every picture runs at 20 pictures a second for a second or two; a scene seen for the very first time can drop to 13-19 pictures a second while the driver compiles its vertex shaders (15-38 s each, once).
